summary: Phase 3 implements rule-driven approval gates, durable autonomous-advance receipts, restart-safe milestone proof, receipt acceptance across downstream consumers, the default config template, and the pinned semantic journeys. The recorded verification is green: typecheck; 33 generated schemas; 1,220 unit tests; 511 contract tests; 231 integration tests after rebuilding the bundle; 35 crash tests; and 9 focused release/install tests. Independent review reported one non-blocking major concern: the task-local D9 self-application cutover is not part of the claimable phase output, so the phase commit alone temporarily leaves this task on its prior config. I rejected that as a defect in the reviewed phase subject because fresh server status blocks while the digest-pinned task config is edited and task-config paths cannot be claimed by the implementation manifest. The deviation is explicit in the implementation notes: after the authorized phase commit is observed, this same session will reapply the exact D9 approval_rules and header refresh and commit them with state.json and authority records before any successor is reported or started. The human must decide whether that documented two-commit sequence is an acceptable material deviation from the approved in-phase cutover.
